benchmark.category: an open-world GTA-style single-file browser game set on a college campus
benchmark.users: hackathon judges and student players who open the preview link on desktop and on their own phones to play the five daily campus missions and meet the story characters

requirements.source_phrase: The goal is that the game loads, the world shows up, the controls respond and nothing crashes on startup.
requirements.statement: Opening the preview link loads the game from the uploaded zip: the start screen renders and the player can enter the world, with no blank page, build error or crash on load
requirements.notes: Phase 1 goal of the approved plan; the game is one static HTML file with inline audio, so load means the file and its assets are served and the script runs.

requirements.source_phrase: The goal is that the game loads, the world shows up, the controls respond and nothing crashes on startup.
requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns the whole single-file game with status 200 and every sub-resource it requests on load (audio, images) returns 200 with non-zero bytes
requirements.notes: No application server exists; the static hosting layer plus the browser-local save are the only backend surfaces, so the check is on the served document and its asset responses.

requirements.statement: GET / on the preview host lands the browser on the game (a redirect or the served game itself) so the main preview link opens the start screen with no extra click and no 404
requirements.notes: Build description: the main preview link opens straight to the GATE-6 start screen and App.js redirects / to /game/index.html.

requirements.statement: On the start screen the player can type a name, pick a character and press Play, and the world loads with that character under the player's control
requirements.notes: Build description: the start screen has a name field, character select and Play; the start button has a pulse animation, so clicks may need to be forced. The plan only says 'menu or straight into the world', so the exact labels stay open.

requirements.statement: The page records the entered name and chosen character in the save object (localStorage key gate6.save.v1) before gameplay and restores them on the next load
requirements.notes: Saves live in localStorage gate6.save.v1 per the build description; clearing that key is the documented fresh start.

requirements.source_phrase: Play with the project's existing controls.
requirements.statement: On desktop, W, A, S and D move the player in their four directions, E interacts with the nearby interactable and Space triggers SLAP, each producing its action and leaving the page unscrolled
requirements.notes: The plan targets a desktop browser with keyboard and mouse; the specific WASD/E/Space bindings come from the build description and README.

requirements.source_phrase: Play with the project's existing controls.
requirements.statement: The served document binds those keys in its key handler, each handler runs without an uncaught error, and no binding navigates the page away or scrolls the document
requirements.notes: Key handling lives inside the single served file; the failure modes are a throwing handler or a default browser action such as space-scroll.

requirements.source_phrase: The game's existing features stay as they are: no new features, no redesign and no content changes.
requirements.statement: Every screen the game already had (start, tutorial, play HUD, pause, mission briefing, result card) keeps its original layout, copy, art and controls apart from the Bawalverse rename and the phone-landscape layout fix
requirements.notes: The plan limits changes to what makes the game run; later user turns add the rename and the mobile touch fixes, which are the only sanctioned departures.

requirements.source_phrase: The game's existing features stay as they are: no new features, no redesign and no content changes.
requirements.statement: The served files carry the uploaded game's own code with changes confined to the branding strings and the phone-landscape CSS; the mission table, world data and control handlers are otherwise the uploaded versions
requirements.notes: Derived from the plan's change limit; hard to test mechanically, so check the mission table, world arrays and handlers for rewrites.

requirements.source_phrase: The game keeps its original look, sound and controls.
requirements.statement: After the player presses Play the game's built-in music and sound effects play through the page's audio with no console error and are audible during the opening and a SLAP
requirements.notes: The developer agent never checked sound; browsers block audio before a gesture, so Play is the gate.

requirements.source_phrase: The game keeps its original look, sound and controls.
requirements.statement: Every audio source the game references is embedded in the served file and resolves, and playback is not blocked after the user's first gesture
requirements.notes: A missing embedded asset or an autoplay policy error would show as a console error rather than a visible break.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: On a 390x844 touch phone, dragging the on-screen stick moves the player in the dragged direction, and tapping SLAP, E and RUN each performs its action within a moment
requirements.notes: Use is_mobile+has_touch contexts; the build names #stickbase, #btnSlap, #btnE and #btnRun, and the Pitch beats are tapped.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: The served page binds touch handlers to #stickbase, #btnSlap, #btnE and #btnRun and the touch path calls the same player actions as the keyboard path without an uncaught error
requirements.notes: A touch handler that throws or fires on pointerdown twice would make the button feel dead or double-fire.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: At 390x844 and 360x640 no HUD control overlaps another or is clipped off-screen, and every action button is fully visible and tappable
requirements.notes: Layout class check; the original game was built desktop-first and mobile was out of phase 1 until this user line.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: The served document declares a mobile viewport and contains portrait CSS that lays out the stick, action buttons and right-hand buttons within a 360 px wide viewport with no horizontal document overflow
requirements.notes: Check window.innerWidth and document.scrollWidth at 360 px; a missing viewport meta makes the page scale instead of fit.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: At 844x390 and 740x360 the right-hand buttons, minimap, mission card, stick and action buttons do not overlap or clip, each is visible and tappable, and the mission card's text is legible rather than washed out
requirements.notes: The developer agent reported the right-hand column overlapped E/RUN and help was cut off, and says it now sits in a two-column grid under the minimap with the map key hidden; the agent also noted the landscape mission card may look faded and left it unchecked.

requirements.source_phrase: Mobile Touch Check: Make sure the game plays smoothly on phones with touch controls for the judges
requirements.statement: The served document's landscape/short-screen media rules place the right-hand buttons under the minimap, keep E left of SLAP and put the mission card between the stick and the action buttons, and the page reports no element wider than the viewport at 844x390 and 740x360
requirements.notes: The agent's claimed layout is the mechanism the user's 'smoothly on phones' line depends on; Phase 4 checks the rules apply at those viewports.

requirements.source_phrase: Replace the game name with Bawalverse
requirements.statement: The browser tab title, the big title on the start screen and the pause menu caption all show the product name Bawalverse
requirements.notes: User's rename instruction; the developer agent's summary does not mention carrying it out, so it is unverified.

requirements.source_phrase: Replace the game name with Bawalverse
requirements.statement: The served index.html and gate6-campus-rush.html both contain Bawalverse in the <title> and in the start-screen and pause-menu markup, with no leftover product name in those three surfaces
requirements.notes: String check on the served files; the two copies must agree.

requirements.source_phrase: add one tagline
requirements.statement: Exactly one tagline line sits directly under the BAWALVERSE title on the start screen, and no second tagline appears anywhere on that screen
requirements.notes: 'one tagline' is the only constraint the user gave; the wording is checked by brand-strings-fe.

requirements.source_phrase: add one tagline
requirements.statement: The served start-screen markup holds exactly one tagline element directly under the title element, and the pause and world screens hold none
requirements.notes: Prevents a tagline duplicated into the HUD or pause menu.

requirements.statement: The tab title reads 'Bawalverse — Bawal hai. Karna padega.', the start screen shows BAWALVERSE with VERSE in gold, the tagline 'Bawal hai. Karna padega.' under it and the kicker 'Bawalverse · day after day'
requirements.notes: Exact strings come from the build description's branding checklist; the user asked only for the name and one tagline, so these values are the build's narrowing of that request.

requirements.statement: The served file contains those exact strings in the <title> and in the start-screen markup
requirements.notes: Character-exact string check, including the em dash and middle dot.

requirements.statement: The in-world place names 'Gate-6' gate, 'Gate-6 Gazette' and 'GATE-6 KART CLUB' still read as before, so the rename touched only the product name
requirements.notes: From 'no content changes' plus the rename scope: these are campus places, not the product name, and a blanket find-and-replace would wrongly change them.

requirements.statement: Those three in-world strings still appear unchanged in the served file
requirements.notes: Over-broad rename detection; also checks the rename did not delete the gate sign or the kart club.

requirements.source_phrase: Play through all five daily missions on phone and desktop and fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: On desktop each of the five daily missions opens its briefing, starts, shows its HUD objective and timer, and reaches its result card by being completed or failed, after which the game keeps running with no uncaught JS error and input still responding
requirements.notes: The task input names the five: Chai Run (chai), Yulu Time Trial (yulu), Crowd Control (crowd), The Recovery (recovery), The Pitch (pitch). Walking is slow, so teleporting via P.x/P.y and driving mxBrief/mxStart/mxFinish/mxFail through page.evaluate is accepted, with real input where practical.

requirements.source_phrase: Play through all five daily missions on phone and desktop and fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: The served file defines the five missions and their mxStart/mxFinish/mxFail transitions run without throwing; finishing or failing records the outcome in the save and frees the player for the next mission
requirements.notes: Mission state lives in MX with definitions in MXT, reachable from page.evaluate as top-level consts.

requirements.source_phrase: Play through all five daily missions on phone and desktop and fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: On a 390x844 touch phone each of the five missions can be briefed, started, tracked in the HUD and completed or failed using the touch controls, with every card and button visible, tappable and unoverlapped
requirements.notes: Same sweep on the touch path; a mission card that cannot be reached or a confirm button behind another button is a break.

requirements.source_phrase: Play through all five daily missions on phone and desktop and fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: The touch path starts and ends all five missions through the same mission functions as the desktop path with no uncaught error, and the outcome is saved
requirements.notes: Check the saved mission state after a touch-path finish, not only that the card changed.

requirements.statement: The mission table defines exactly five Tier-1 daily missions: Chai Run (chai), Yulu Time Trial (yulu), Crowd Control (crowd), The Recovery (recovery) and The Pitch (pitch)
requirements.notes: Mission ids and names come from the build description and the task's sweep list; Phase 4 checks MXT holds exactly these five.

requirements.statement: Opening /game/gate6-campus-rush.html shows the same Bawalverse branding and the same phone-landscape layout as /game/index.html
requirements.notes: The developer agent states the landscape change was made in both copies so they match; the rename happened after and may have missed one.

requirements.statement: The two served files are identical in their branding strings and phone-landscape CSS, so a fix in one is present in the other
requirements.notes: Diff the changed regions of index.html and gate6-campus-rush.html.

requirements.source_phrase: fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: Across one full session -- load, start, tutorial, all five missions, pause, store and a reload -- the page raises no uncaught JS error and never freezes with input dead
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'nothing crashes on startup': the crash the user cares about is mid-mission. Collect page.on('pageerror') for the whole sweep.

requirements.source_phrase: fix anything that breaks
requirements.statement: The scripted sweep produces zero pageerror events and the game loop's frame counter keeps increasing after each mission ends
requirements.notes: A frozen requestAnimationFrame loop is the softlock the user would report.

requirements.statement: Failing a mission (timer expiry or a failed objective) shows the fail result card, leaves the wallet unchanged, and returns the player to free play able to start another mission
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'mission can be completed or failed': the half-written failure is a mission stuck open with the HUD still counting.

requirements.statement: mxFail clears the current mission, credits no pay and leaves the saved wallet as it was
requirements.notes: Read the save after the forced fail to confirm no payout was written.

requirements.statement: Opening the pause menu stops player movement and mission time, and resuming closes it, returns the player to the same spot and continues the mission timer from where it paused
requirements.notes: The build lists a pause menu; the unstated half is that resuming does not lose the mission or warp the player.

requirements.statement: While paused the mission timer does not decrement and the player position is unchanged; on resume the timer continues and the paused flag is stored as off
requirements.notes: A timer that keeps running while paused turns a pause into a silent mission failure.

requirements.statement: The tutorial opens on a first play, advances through its steps with the real controls, can be exited at any point with its Skip tutorial button, and afterwards leaves the player in free play with nothing blocking the screen
requirements.notes: Build description: a tutorial card with a Skip tutorial button (#tut); the unstated half is that skipping neither traps the player nor replays the tutorial constantly.

requirements.statement: The save records that the tutorial was seen, so a reload after completing or skipping it goes straight to free play
requirements.notes: Check the tutorial flag in gate6.save.v1 rather than only the on-screen card.

requirements.statement: After earning mission pay and completing a mission, reloading the page restores the same name, character, wallet balance and mission completion marks
requirements.notes: Build description: progress saves in localStorage key gate6.save.v1 and clearing that key is a fresh start.

requirements.statement: localStorage key gate6.save.v1 holds name, character, wallet and mission state, is rewritten on each change, and a profile with the key cleared starts at day 1 with the default wallet
requirements.notes: There is no server, so the save record is the whole persistence layer.

requirements.statement: A malformed, partial or foreign value in gate6.save.v1 does not blank the game: the page loads the start screen with default state and rewrites the key
requirements.notes: Paranoid persistence check; an unguarded JSON.parse on the load path throws and leaves a black canvas.

requirements.statement: The mission card lists the five daily missions by name and marks the ones completed today, with the running mission marked while it is active
requirements.notes: Build description: five daily missions and a mission card, which sits at the bottom on landscape phones.

requirements.statement: The mission definitions supply the five names and the stored completion state the card reads back after a reload
requirements.notes: The card is only as right as the saved completion state it reads.

requirements.statement: The wallet HUD shows the stored balance and increases by exactly the pay the result card states the moment a mission completes
requirements.notes: Business-logic class: the displayed balance, the result card's pay and the stored number must agree.

requirements.statement: The stored balance equals the sum of all credited mission pay minus store purchases, in whole currency units, and a reload reads back the same number
requirements.notes: Compare the save value with the sum of the payouts the result cards showed.

requirements.statement: A running mission's timer decrements once per real second from the mission's defined duration, stops at zero and triggers the fail path exactly once
requirements.notes: Domain rule behind the HUD timer the sweep reads; a timer that double-fires or runs backwards fails the mission twice.

requirements.statement: At 1920x800 the start screen and the character select fit the viewport without clipping, and the Play button is visible without scrolling or opening a menu
requirements.notes: Layout class: primary action must start visible; the plan's target is a desktop browser.

requirements.statement: The served page's CSS keeps the start and character-select panels inside a 1920x800 viewport with no horizontal scroll and no element past the viewport edge
requirements.notes: Measure document.scrollWidth against innerWidth.

requirements.statement: The BAWALVERSE title, the tagline, the Play button label and the HUD objective text each meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against their immediate background
requirements.notes: Layout/visual class; the gold VERSE on a dark field and the faded landscape mission card are the likely failures.

requirements.statement: The colour pairs declared for those texts in the served CSS compute to at least 4.5:1
requirements.notes: Compute from the CSS values when the rendered pixel sample is unreliable.

requirements.statement: Every action answers on screen: pressing Play leaves the start screen within a second, a mission result card says whether it passed and what it paid, and a store purchase that cannot be afforded says so instead of doing nothing
requirements.notes: Class requirement that nothing succeeds or fails silently; the store case is the one most likely to look live but do nothing.

requirements.statement: Play, mission finish/fail and a refused purchase each change on-screen state (screen change, result card, refusal message), and no path ends silently with the same view as before
requirements.notes: A control that renders but does not change state is the failure this catches.

requirements.statement: The trophy, store, map and help buttons each open their panel over the game, and closing it returns to the play screen with the player's position and wallet unchanged
requirements.notes: Build description lists right-hand buttons for trophy, store, map and help; the landscape fix hides the map key, so the remaining three still need to open.

requirements.statement: Each panel's open/close is driven by game state that resets on close, and opening a panel while a mission runs does not lose the mission
requirements.notes: A panel left flagged open would freeze input after closing the overlay.

requirements.statement: The game requires no sign-in and sends no progress to a server: a second browser profile or a private window opens a fresh game with no access to another player's save, and no player data leaves the browser
requirements.notes: Access-control class for a product with no accounts: the boundary is the browser's own localStorage, per the build description's 'no server or database'.

requirements.statement: A mission payout, a purchase or a mission completion is written to gate6.save.v1 before the next render, so closing the tab immediately afterwards and reopening shows the same balance and marks
requirements.notes: Persistence class: a save written only on exit loses the last payout when a judge closes the tab.

requirements.source_phrase: catch the voice and place it
requirements.statement: In Adhiraj's office scenes every fixed line — the openers, the mid-beat reactions, the apologies, the closings and the brushoff — is heard in the cloned voice made from the uploaded recording, audible and non-empty, with no fixed line still played by the old stand-in voice
requirements.notes: Replaces the stand-in-only contract of this requirement with the cloned voice the user supplied and approved. Browsers block audio before a gesture, so the office must be entered by a key press or tap first; the caller checks audible playback and no console error, not just that markup exists.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the stand-in voice for those
requirements.statement: The stand-in voice path is kept for office lines whose text carries a teammate's name or the visit number, and for any fixed line whose clip is missing or fails to load; each line plays exactly one source, the clip or the stand-in but never both, and the fallback yields a non-empty utterance or its subtitle so the scene advances instead of hanging
requirements.notes: From the user's answer on how lines with a teammate's name or a visit number should sound; the missing-clip half is the paranoid form so a 404 or an empty file cannot dead-end the scene, and the one-source rule catches clip and speech synthesis playing over each other.

requirements.statement: On a phone the player moves within about 100 ms of dragging the stick, and after opening and closing the pause, trophy, store, map and help panels ten times the controls respond as fast as the first time
requirements.notes: Performance class: 'plays smoothly' is the user's line; lag after repeated overlays is the usual web-game leak.

requirements.statement: Repeated panel opens and pause/resume leave one running game loop and one mission timer; the timer does not accelerate and no duplicate input handler accumulates
requirements.notes: Count requestAnimationFrame loops and touch listeners before and after the repeats.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html and GET /game/gate6-campus-rush.html both return 200 with the complete game, and the browser console shows no missing-module, undefined-name or 404 error on load or during the first mission
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class: the game is a static file behind the preview host, so a bad path or an undefined global is the realistic break.

requirements.statement: While a mission runs the HUD shows the current objective text, the remaining time and the wallet, and those values change as the mission progresses
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games carry a persistent HUD with objective, timer and money; players read mission state from it without opening a menu.

requirements.statement: The HUD values are read from live mission and wallet state each frame rather than from a snapshot taken at mission start
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- a HUD frozen at mission start misreports the timer

requirements.statement: The store opens with items and prices, a purchase deducts the price from the wallet and marks the item owned, and an unaffordable item is refused with a visible reason
requirements.notes: benchmark: a game with a wallet always has somewhere to spend it; the store button is in the build.

requirements.statement: A purchase debits exactly the listed price once, marks the item owned in the save and cannot be repeated for the same item
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- double-charging on a fast double tap is the classic money bug

requirements.statement: The trophy panel lists the game's trophies with an earned or unearned state, and a trophy earned in a mission shows as earned there
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- a trophy button opens an achievement list whose entries change when earned.

requirements.statement: Earning a trophy writes it to the save, and the panel reads that state back after a reload
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- achievements that vanish on reload are not achievements

requirements.statement: The help panel lists the controls for the device in use: keyboard keys on desktop, the stick and action buttons on a phone
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- help shows the controls the current device actually has, not a desktop-only list

requirements.statement: The controls the help panel lists match the handlers the page actually binds on that device
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- help text that names keys the game does not bind misleads judges

requirements.statement: The minimap renders the campus, moves the player's marker as the player moves, and shows the active mission's marker while one runs
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world games always answer 'where am I and where is the objective' on a minimap; the build has one and the mission sweep relies on mission markers.

requirements.statement: The minimap is drawn from world coordinates each frame with the player position mapped into its bounds, so a teleported player's marker moves with them
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world browser games -- a minimap that does not track the player is a static picture

requirements.source_phrase: catch the voice and place it
requirements.statement: The served game maps each of the 25 fixed office line ids (open-1..open-5, mid-1..mid-9, apo-1..apo-4, again-2, again-3, close-long, close-quiet, close-apo, close-default, brushoff) to assets/adhiraj/<id>.mp3, and each of those URLs returns 200 or 206 with Content-Type audio/mpeg and non-zero bytes, so no fixed office line plays from a missing or empty file
requirements.notes: The 25 ids come from the build description (files_of_reference /app/frontend/public/game/assets/adhiraj/*.mp3). Fetch each file directly to prove it is served non-empty; a clip that 404s would silently fall back and hide the missing voice.

requirements.source_phrase: Make sure he says the same thing as in the current game; only the voice changes to the attached one.
requirements.statement: Every office line's on-screen text — the opener, the mid-beat reactions, the choice replies and the closing line — reads exactly as it did before the voice change, and that text is on screen while its audio plays
requirements.notes: The user forbids content changes; a line whose subtitle was rewritten to match the recording's original words fails this. Compare against the pre-change DIR_* strings, not against the audio.

requirements.source_phrase: Make sure he says the same thing as in the current game; only the voice changes to the attached one.
requirements.statement: The served index.html still holds the DIR_OPEN, DIR_MID, DIR_REACT and dirClosing strings unchanged from before the voice change, and each clip id the generation script lists corresponds to that line's text
requirements.notes: The line text per id is listed in /app/scripts/adhiraj_voice.py; character-exact comparison of the strings is mechanical, while the audio-to-text correspondence needs a listening check and is the hard half.

requirements.source_phrase: only the voice changes to the attached one
requirements.statement: Entering the office, choosing Apologise, Blame or Say nothing at each beat, hearing a closing line and leaving the office follow the same sequence, choices, rewards and star clearing as before, with only the audio changed
requirements.notes: The user's change limit; the risk is that swapping the voice path rewrote beat logic or dropped a branch.

requirements.source_phrase: only the voice changes to the attached one
requirements.statement: dirEnter, dirChoose and dirClosing keep the same branches, rewards and wanted-star clearing as before the voice change, with the only code difference on the voice playback path
requirements.notes: Read the office functions in the served file and diff the beat table against the pre-change version; judge by branches and reward values, not by formatting.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the stand-in voice for those
requirements.statement: An office line whose text contains a teammate's name or the visit number is heard through the browser stand-in voice with its text on screen, and the scene moves on to the next beat without hanging
requirements.notes: The user's explicit exception; the failure it guards is a blame reaction or blame closing that selects no clip and then never resolves, leaving the scene stuck.

requirements.statement: With at least one wanted star, entering the office plays an opener, accepts a choice at each beat, plays a closing line after Leave the office is chosen, returns to free play with the wanted stars cleared, and every line's typewriter text finishes so the scene cannot stall, with no uncaught JS error
requirements.notes: Build description: office entry needs wantedLevel()>=1 and the scene runs open → mid → close with typewriter text. The continuity note gives the page.evaluate shortcut (S.stars=2; S.dirT=-999; dirEnter()) for reaching the office quickly.

requirements.statement: dirEnter with wantedLevel() >= 1 advances the scene through the beats to a closing line, dirChoose records the option picked at each beat, leaving resets the office state so the next visit starts fresh and clears the wanted stars, and no pageerror is raised during the flow
requirements.notes: Check the office flags and wanted level after leaving, not only the on-screen card; a flag left set is the softlock the user reported for other scenes.

requirements.statement: Entering the office with zero wanted stars plays the brushoff line and no reaction or closing line, then returns the player to free play, on desktop and on a phone
requirements.notes: Build description: with 0 stars dirEnter() plays the brushoff ('Do you need something?'); the item exercises that clip file in the shipped voice set.

requirements.statement: dirEnter with wantedLevel() === 0 selects the brushoff clip and runs no reaction or closing branch, leaving the wanted level and the stored save unchanged
requirements.notes: The brushoff path was previously the whole feature; the risk is the new voice code running beats even at 0 stars.

requirements.statement: The second office visit plays the again-2 opener and the third plays again-3, each with its own text, and the visit count survives a page reload so the same opener is heard again after reloading
requirements.notes: Build description: again-2 and again-3 are the second and third visit openers and S.dirUses counts visits. Two visits in one session and one after a reload are both needed.

requirements.statement: The save's office visit counter increments once per office entry, is read back after a reload, and selects again-2 on visit 2 and again-3 on visit 3 while visit 4 and later fall through to the visit-number line rather than replaying a fixed opener
requirements.notes: Guards against a counter that increments per beat (skipping again-2 to a later opener) or resets on reload.

requirements.statement: While an office clip is playing the voice label beside the scene reads 'his voice (AI-recreated)', and the label names no other speaker during that playback
requirements.notes: Build description: #ofvoice shows 'his voice (AI-recreated)' while a clip plays; the user's permission answer is what the 'AI-recreated' wording credits.

requirements.statement: The served markup contains 'his voice (AI-recreated)' bound to the #ofvoice label, set when a clip starts and cleared or returned to its idle text when the clip ends
requirements.notes: Character-exact string check plus a check the label is not permanently stuck on after the scene ends.

requirements.statement: Pause menu → Audio mixer shows a note stating that Adhiraj's voice is an AI recreation made with his permission
requirements.notes: Build description: the mixer note (~5155) mentions the AI recreation made with permission; the user answered 'Yes, he has agreed' to the consent question, which is what the note records in the product.

requirements.statement: The served markup for the audio mixer panel contains that note text naming the AI recreation and the permission, and the panel still opens from the pause menu with the game's other sound settings
requirements.notes: String check on the served file; keep the mixer otherwise unchanged so the note does not replace the volume controls.

requirements.source_phrase: Emergent managed voice cloning
requirements.statement: Adhiraj's voice is created with Emergent managed voice cloning and the 25 clips are shipped inside the served app, so playing an office line makes no request to an external voice service and needs no key or credential
requirements.notes: The user chose the service; the build description (other_misc_info) says the cloning is pre-generated with no runtime API. Test by loading the office with network calls to outside hosts blocked after page load — the scene must still be voiced.

requirements.statement: Every voiced office line shows its subtitle text while the audio plays, and setting the mixer's voice volume to zero silences the line while the scene still advances through its beats
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games always subtitle voiced lines and put their volume under the game's own audio mixer, so a player with sound off or on a muted phone can follow the scene.

requirements.statement: Each clip's playback is routed through the mixer's voice gain node or volume setting, so a zeroed voice volume produces silence for the clip without blocking line advance, and muting the other channels leaves the voice audible
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games — a voice channel the mixer does not control, or one that stalls the scene when muted, is the usual bug.

requirements.statement: The campus map shows each of today's uncompleted missions as a coloured dot labelled with that mission's name, and a mission already completed today has no dot
requirements.notes: Build description: the map now marks uncompleted daily missions as coloured dots with their names. Distinct from the inherited active-mission marker on the minimap.

requirements.statement: The map reads each mission's position and today's completion state from the mission table and the save, so a dot disappears once its mission is completed and stays gone after a reload
requirements.notes: Check the dot list against the five mission positions and the saved completion marks, not only that dots render.

requirements.statement: Switching tabs or taking a call during The Pitch pauses the beat sequence, and on return the remaining beats play on from where they stopped with none counted as missed for the time away
requirements.notes: Build description: the pitch now pauses when the tab is hidden, fixing a lose-your-mission bug. Simulate with document.hidden / a tab switch and check the beat index and the mission outcome.

requirements.statement: The Pitch's beat scheduler stops advancing while the page is hidden and resumes at the same beat when the page becomes visible, so its outcome matches an uninterrupted run
requirements.notes: A paused pitch that still decrements its own timer would expire while hidden; compare the mission result with and without a hidden interval of the same length.

requirements.statement: The Yulu Time Trial result shows the run's leaderboard rank as a whole number of at least 1 and never as '#0', including for a slow run
requirements.notes: Build description: a slower run used to display rank '#0' and now shows the correct rank; test with a deliberately slow finish.

requirements.statement: The rank is computed from the run's recorded time against the stored leaderboard times and clamped to at least 1, so a slower run shows a lower rank rather than zero
requirements.notes: Business-logic class on the mission result; the seeded times must be compared, since a single run has no position among zero competitors.

requirements.statement: At 390x844 portrait the running mission's countdown is fully readable near the top of the screen and is not covered by the mission card, the stick or the action buttons
requirements.notes: Build description: on upright phones the countdown now sits near the top because it used to sit behind the mission card. Layout check with a mission running.

requirements.statement: The portrait CSS places the mission timer above the mission card in the stacking order and inside the viewport at 390x844 and 360x640
requirements.notes: Check the computed stacking/z-index and the timer's bounding box against the mission card's at both viewports; a rule that only applies in landscape would leave portrait broken.
